newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-ELS AND WESTNER SET THE PACE ON HOME SOIL.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-ELS AND WESTNER SET THE PACE ON HOME SOIL.

text.p: Ernie Els and Wayne Westner set the pace on home soil on the opening day of the World Cup of Golf on Thursday.
Els and Westner each shot 68s to finish the rain-delayed first day on eight under par -- two shots clear of second-placed Denmark.
Defending champions the United States had a disappointing day, with Tom Lehman and Steve Jones shooting 73s.
Low round of the day belonged to Dane Thomas Bjorn who shot 67, although some of the best golf came from Scottish World Cup debutant Paul Lawrie. He had four birdies on the back nine for a 69.
With Andrew Coltart shooting a 70, Scotland ended the day in third place on five under with Argentina and China tied for fourth place on two under.
Heavy rain had delayed the start by three hours, suiting the long hitting South Africans.
"I really enjoyed the golf course playing so long," said Els. "The ball didn't have much roll and the greens were fairer because of the rain. It suited us.
"We started off a little nervy in front of our home crowd and the holes looked a little small for a while."
Bjorn, who had six birdies, said it had helped his game playing with Els and Westner.
"We were really happy to play with them -- it helped our concentration. When they holed out everyone moved on but we just had to keep it together.
"We aimed on being in the top five and now we feel very confident for the next three days."
